MedModr Home
Statistical Software

Mediation, Moderation &
Conditional Process Analysis
done right.

A free, user-friendly, open-source application for mediation, moderation, and conditional process analysis. Runs entirely in your web browser with no installation required and no internet connection needed. Use it offline on any device, anywhere.

1 - 92

Regression

Bootstrap
Percentile + BC
Key Features
Fit Model (Custom Regression)
Build OLS or logistic regressions from your own predictors and interactions, queue multiple models, and estimate them all in one run. Interactions come with conditional-effect tables so you can see how effects change across moderator values.
Data Screening & Diagnostics
Outlier detection (Z-score, IQR, MAD, Percentile), normality tests (skewness, kurtosis), correlation matrix (Pearson, Spearman, Kendall), sample size recommendations, histograms, and Q-Q plots.
Missing Data Handling
Multiple Imputation (PMM), Mean/Median/Mode imputation, Hot Deck, Regression imputation, EM Algorithm, and Listwise deletion.
Categorical Variable Encoding
Automatic detection and dummy coding of categorical variables with user-selectable reference categories.
Data Import & Export
CSV/Excel import, multiple sheet support for Excel, data preview with summary statistics, export cleaned data as CSV, export results as Word, PDF, and HTML.
Data Editor with Recode
Edit data directly in the browser. Reverse code variables (e.g., 1↔5, 2↔4) and recode values (text or numeric) into new columns or replace existing data.
Bootstrap Confidence Intervals
Percentile and Bias-Corrected (BC) bootstrap methods for indirect effects. Adjustable number of bootstrap samples (1,000, 5000, and 10,000).
Path Diagrams
Interactive SVG path diagrams for analysis types. Customizable node shapes, line thickness, colors, and export as PNG/SVG.
Simple Slopes Plots
Simple slopes plots for moderation and moderated mediation. Customizable colors, labels, legend, and high-resolution download.
Publication-Ready Tables
Regression tables include unstandardized (b) and standardized (β) coefficients, SE, t/z, p-values, confidence intervals, and VIF for multicollinearity diagnostics.
Mean Centering Options
Optional and fully manual — nothing is centered automatically. Hand-pick which variables from your role boxes to center, then choose to create new c_-prefixed variables or replace the originals in place. Skip it and analyses use raw values.
Moderator Values
Switch between two probing strategies for moderation and moderated mediation models. Use Mean ± 1 SD for standard simple slopes, or Percentile (16/50/84%) for robust probing when the moderator is skewed or non-normally distributed.
Multiple Variables & Combination Runs
Assign more than one X, M, or Y and every combination is analyzed in a single run — e.g. 2 X × 2 Y produces all model pairs at once with per-combination results and navigation.
Standard Errors: OLS & Robust (HC0–HC4)
Choose classical OLS or heteroskedasticity-consistent robust SEs (HC0–HC4). Coefficients stay the same; SE, t/z, p, CI and F-test are recomputed. Applies to regression tables only.
Regression Diagnostics
Descriptives, dominance analysis, all-subsets regression, residual and influence plots, per-case statistics, and diagnostic tests — all exportable to Word.
Offline & Mobile Ready
Works completely offline. Responsive design works on desktop, iPad/tablet (Android), and mobile devices.
Available Analysis Types (Models)
Fit Model (Custom Regression)
Fit any OLS or logistic regression. Combine predictors, add your own interaction terms, queue multiple models, and run them together.
W moderates X→Y (Model 1)
Tests if the X→Y relationship depends on moderator W (X×W interaction). Includes simple slopes plot. Supports 1 moderator.
W & Z moderate X→Y (Model 2)
Tests if two moderators (W and Z) moderate the X→Y relationship (X×W + X×Z interactions). Supports 2 moderators.
W & Z jointly moderate X→Y (Model 3)
Tests if the X→Y relationship is moderated by a three-way interaction X × W × Z → Y. Supports 2 moderators.
M mediates X→Y (Model 4)
Tests if X → M → Y transmits effect through a single mediator. Includes Sobel test. Supports 1 mediator.
M₁, M₂,... mediate X→Y in parallel (Model 4)
Tests if multiple independent mediators X → {M₁...Mₖ} → Y simultaneously transmit the effect of X on Y. Supports 2-10 mediators.
W moderates X→Y (Model 5)
Tests if moderator W affects only the direct X→Y path (c'-path) in a mediation model. Supports 1–3 mediators.
M₁→M₂→... mediate X→Y in serial (Model 6)
Tests if X affects Y through a causal chain X → M₁ → M₂ → Y with three indirect paths. Supports 2-10 mediators.
W moderates X→M (Model 7)
Tests if the indirect effect depends on W moderating the X→M path (a-path) in a mediation model. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M & X→Y (Model 8)
Tests if the indirect effect depends on W moderating both the X→M path and the direct X→Y path. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W & Z moderate X→M (Model 9)
Tests if W and Z moderate the X→M path simultaneously with separate moderators. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W & Z moderate X→M & X→Y (Model 10)
Tests if W and Z moderate both the X→M path and the direct X→Y path. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W & Z jointly moderate X→M (Model 11)
Tests if W and Z jointly moderate the X→M path with a three-way interaction; Y is predicted by X and M. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W & Z jointly moderate X→M & X→Y (Model 12)
Tests if W and Z jointly moderate both the X→M path and the direct X→Y path with three-way interactions. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W & Z jointly moderate X→M; W moderates X→Y (Model 13)
Tests if W and Z jointly moderate X→M while W moderates X→Y. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates M→Y (Model 14)
Tests if the indirect effect depends on W moderating the M→Y path (b-path) in a mediation model. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates M→Y & X→Y (Model 15)
Tests if W moderates both the M→Y path and the direct X→Y path. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W & Z moderate M→Y (Model 16)
Tests if W and Z moderate the M→Y path; the direct X→Y path is unmoderated. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W & Z moderate M→Y & X→Y (Model 17)
Tests if W and Z moderate both the M→Y path and the direct X→Y path. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W & Z jointly moderate M→Y (Model 18)
Tests if W and Z jointly moderate the M→Y path with a three-way interaction; X→Y is unmoderated. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W & Z jointly moderate M→Y & X→Y (Model 19)
Tests if W and Z jointly moderate both the M→Y path and the direct X→Y path with three-way interactions. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W & Z jointly moderate M→Y; W moderates X→Y (Model 20)
Tests if W and Z jointly moderate M→Y while W moderates X→Y. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M; Z moderates M→Y (Model 21)
Tests if W moderates the X→M path while Z moderates the M→Y path. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M & X→Y; Z moderates M→Y (Model 22)
Tests if W moderates X→M and X→Y while Z moderates M→Y. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M; Z moderates M→Y & X→Y (Model 28)
Tests if W moderates X→M while Z moderates both M→Y and X→Y. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M & X→Y; Z moderates X→M & X→Y (Model 29)
Tests if both W and Z moderate the X→M and X→Y paths. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M & M→Y (Model 58)
Tests if the indirect effect depends on W moderating both the X→M and M→Y paths. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M, M→Y & X→Y (Model 59)
Tests if W moderates all three paths (X→M, M→Y, and X→Y) in a full moderated mediation model. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M & M→Y; Z moderates X→M (Model 60)
Tests if W moderates X→M and M→Y while Z moderates X→M. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M, M→Y & X→Y; Z moderates X→M (Model 61)
Tests if W moderates X→M, M→Y, and X→Y while Z moderates X→M. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M & M→Y; Z moderates X→M & X→Y (Model 62)
Tests if W moderates X→M and M→Y while Z moderates X→M and X→Y. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M, M→Y & X→Y; Z moderates X→M & X→Y (Model 63)
Tests if W moderates X→M, M→Y, and X→Y while Z moderates X→M and X→Y. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M & M→Y; Z moderates M→Y (Model 64)
Tests if W moderates X→M and M→Y while Z moderates M→Y. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M, M→Y & X→Y; Z moderates M→Y (Model 65)
Tests if W moderates X→M, M→Y, and X→Y while Z moderates M→Y. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M & M→Y; Z moderates M→Y & X→Y (Model 66)
Tests if W moderates X→M and M→Y while Z moderates M→Y and X→Y. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M, M→Y & X→Y; Z moderates M→Y & X→Y (Model 67)
Tests if W moderates X→M, M→Y, and X→Y while Z moderates M→Y and X→Y. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W & Z jointly moderate X→M; W moderates M→Y (Model 68)
Tests if W and Z jointly moderate X→M while W moderates M→Y. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W & Z jointly moderate X→M & X→Y; W moderates M→Y (Model 69)
Tests if W and Z jointly moderate X→M and X→Y while W moderates M→Y. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M; W & Z jointly moderate M→Y (Model 70)
Tests if W moderates X→M while W and Z jointly moderate M→Y. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M; W & Z jointly moderate M→Y & X→Y (Model 71)
Tests if W moderates X→M while W and Z jointly moderate M→Y and X→Y. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W & Z jointly moderate X→M & M→Y (Model 72)
Tests if W and Z jointly moderate both the X→M and M→Y paths. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W & Z jointly moderate X→M, M→Y & X→Y (Model 73)
Tests if W and Z jointly moderate all three paths: X→M, M→Y, and X→Y. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W & Z moderate X→M & M→Y (Model 75)
Tests if W and Z moderate both the X→M path and the M→Y path. Supports 1–3 mediators.
W & Z moderate X→M, M→Y & X→Y (Model 76)
Tests if W and Z moderate all three paths: X→M, M→Y, and X→Y. Supports 1–3 mediators.
M₁, M₂, M₃,... mediate X→Y in parallel & serial (Model 80)
Tests if multiple mediators transmit the effect of X on Y through both parallel and serial paths. Supports 3-6 mediators.
M₁, M₂, M₃,... mediate X→Y in parallel & serial (Model 81)
Tests a combined parallel-serial mediation where M₁ is the first-stage mediator predicted by X, and every subsequent mediator is predicted by both X and M₁. Supports 3-6 mediators.
M₁, M₂, M₃, & M₄ mediate X→Y in parallel & serial (Model 82)
Tests a four-mediator serial-parallel model where M₁ and M₃ are parallel mediators predicted by X, M₂ is predicted by X and M₁, and M₄ is predicted by X and M₃. Requires exactly 4 mediators.
W moderates X→M₁ in serial mediation (Model 83)
Tests if W moderates the first stage of serial mediation (X→M₁→M₂→Y). Supports 2–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M₁ and X→M₂ in serial mediation (Model 84)
Tests if W moderates the first stage (X→M₁) and the second stage (M₁→M₂) of serial mediation. Supports 2–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M₁, X→M₂, and X→Y in serial mediation (Model 85)
Tests if W moderates the first stage, second stage, and direct path in a serial mediation model. Supports 2–3 mediators.
W moderates X→M₁ and X→Y in serial mediation (Model 86)
Tests if W moderates the first stage (X→M₁) and the direct X→Y path in serial mediation. Supports 2–3 mediators.
W moderates M₂→Y in serial mediation (Model 87)
Tests if W moderates the final mediator→outcome path (M₂→Y) in serial mediation. Supports 2–3 mediators.
W moderates M₁→Y and M₂→Y in serial mediation (Model 88)
Tests if W moderates all mediator→outcome paths (M₁→Y and M₂→Y) in serial mediation. Supports 2–3 mediators.
W moderates M₁→Y, M₂→Y, and X→Y in serial mediation (Model 89)
Tests if W moderates all mediator→outcome paths and the direct X→Y path in serial mediation. Supports 2–3 mediators.
W moderates M₂→Y and X→Y in serial mediation (Model 90)
Tests if W moderates the final mediator→outcome path (M₂→Y) and the direct X→Y path in serial mediation. Supports 2–3 mediators.
W moderates M₁→M₂ in serial mediation (Model 91)
Tests if W moderates the intermediary stage (M₁→M₂) in a serial mediation chain. Supports 2–3 mediators.
W moderates all paths in serial mediation (Model 92)
Tests if W moderates every path in the serial mediation chain: X→M₁, M₁→M₂, M₂→Y, and X→Y. Supports 2–3 mediators.

Author

👨‍💻
Mudasir Mohammed Ibrahim

Mudasir Mohammed Ibrahim is a Ghanaian nurse, researcher, data analyst, and open-source advocate 🇬🇭. He is the creator of MedModr, a free tool designed to make commonly used mediation, moderation, and conditional process analysis methods accessible to researchers, students, educators, and practitioners worldwide. His work promotes open science, reproducible research, and equitable access to high-quality statistical tools, especially in underfunded and resource-limited settings.
